summary: Remote-controlled shell/PTY daemon over WebSocket gateway in heavily obfuscated bundle
details: @whalent/agent ships a daemon (invoked as `whalent --token`) whose declared behavior is to connect to a `wss://` gateway and execute commands received from that gateway on the operator's host. The main entry `dist/index.cjs` and the 13.6 MB `dist/core.cjs` bundle `ws`, `node-pty`, `@xterm/headless`, `ssh2`, and `child_process.spawn`/`execFile`, wired through a `handleMessage` dispatcher — a WebSocket-message-to-spawn/PTY dataflow that gives the remote gateway full interactive shell control of any host running the daemon (README states the gateway can issue `upgrade` and `restart` commands, among others). Both bundles are javascript-obfuscator output (rotated 1412-entry string array, `_0xNNNN` identifiers, ~1801 decoder-wrapper inlines, control-flow flattening) produced by the declared `javascript-obfuscator` devDependency, so the exact set of commands the gateway can invoke and any additional message handlers cannot be audited from the shipped artifact. The gateway URL is operator-supplied via `--token`, but the trust model concentrates full-host RCE at whoever controls the gateway endpoint, and the obfuscation prevents the installer from verifying that no additional hardcoded destinations, credentials, or exec paths exist.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
